staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this checked-out vulnerable snapshot. Sample metadata labels vulnerable commit `4391214fa1168f8f7b12a1eca115d76fa07466c3`, but the line-exact anchors below were resolved against the staged ARVO workspace commit above, whose `src/flb_parser_logfmt.c` and `src/flb_unescape.c` line map matches the saved ASan trace and the staged patch.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42483517 (fluent-bit): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target parse_logfmt_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42483517
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The exact 5-byte witness `ff 3d 22 5c 30` is passed by `parse_logfmt_fuzzer` into a plain logfmt parser with no type table. `logfmt_parser()` treats byte `0xff` as a one-byte key, then parses the remainder as `="\\0` with an opening quote, a backslash, and a single trailing octal digit but no closing quote. That produces `value = "\\0"`, `value_escape = FLB_TRUE`, and `value_len = 2`, so the untyped string path allocates `out_str` and calls `flb_unescape_string_utf8()` on the two-byte value slice. `flb_unescape_string_utf8()` sees backslash followed by `'0'`, falls into its default escape path, and calls `u8_read_escape_sequence()` on the one-byte suffix starting at the final input byte. Inside `u8_read_escape_sequence()`, the octal branch copies that first digit and then immediately evaluates `octal_digit(str[i])` with `i == 1` even though only one byte was valid. The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow read of size 1 at `src/flb_unescape.c:96`. The staged patch fixes this by threading the remaining escape length into `u8_read_escape_sequence()`, adding `i < size` guards to each digit-scan loop, and avoiding the helper when no bytes remain after the backslash.

source.description: First project parser step on the vulnerable path. `logfmt_parser()` turns the attacker-controlled first byte into a non-empty key slice and advances `c` to the `=` delimiter, keeping this pair on the value-parsing path.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is 5 bytes `ff 3d 22 5c 30`. Because `ident_byte[0xff] == 1` in this parser table, byte 0 becomes the one-byte key and `key_len = 1` when the scan stops at `=`; that non-empty key is the first project-materialized state required to reach the later quoted-value and unescape logic.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. After consuming the first octal digit, the continuation test probes `str[i]` for another digit but the helper has no remaining-length parameter and no `i < size` guard. On the witnessed path `i == 1` while only one byte was valid, so this condition reads beyond the provided slice.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this exact condition to `i < size && octal_digit(str[i]) && dno < 3` and threads `size` from `flb_unescape_string_utf8()` into `u8_read_escape_sequence()`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. Evaluating `octal_digit(str[i])` dereferences `str[1]`, which is the byte immediately to the right of the 5-byte libFuzzer input allocation.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `READ of size 1` at `/src/fluent-bit/src/flb_unescape.c:96:30` on address `0x6020000000b5`, 0 bytes to the right of region `[0x6020000000b0, 0x6020000000b5)`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant slice is the quoted value bytes. For the exact witness, this parser step materializes `value` as bytes `5c 30` (`\\0`), marks `value_escape = FLB_TRUE`, and computes `value_len = 2` even though the quote is unterminated.

parser_admitted.description: Project dispatch checkpoint into the vulnerable logfmt parser.
parser_admitted.condition: The staged harness creates the parser with format `logfmt`, so `parser->type == FLB_PARSER_LOGFMT` and `flb_parser_do()` dispatches the exact 5-byte witness into `flb_parser_logfmt_do()`.

fine_trace.note: The harness creates a plain logfmt parser with no type table (`types_len == 0`) and passes the exact 5-byte witness directly into `flb_parser_do()`.

Source. The parser treats input byte `0xff` as an identifier byte, so `key` aliases the first testcase byte and `key_len = 1` when `c` stops at `=`. That non-empty key is the first project-materialized state that keeps this pair on the vulnerable path.

After the `=` delimiter, the quoted-value branch advances past `"`, sets `value = c`, and scans bytes `5c 30` (`\\0`). Encountering the backslash sets `value_escape = FLB_TRUE`; the loop then advances over `'0'` to `end`, so `value_len = 2` even though there is no closing quote.

Because the harness parser has `types_len == 0`, the plain string path is used. With `key_len > 0`, `value_len > 0`, and `value_escape == FLB_TRUE`, the code allocates `out_str` and calls `flb_unescape_string_utf8()` on the two-byte value slice from step 2.

On the first iteration, `in_buf` points to the backslash and `sz == 2`. `next = in_buf + 1` therefore points to the only remaining byte `'0'`. Because `*next` is not one of the explicitly handled escapes, the default branch calls `u8_read_escape_sequence()` on that one-byte suffix without supplying any remaining-length bound.

The helper receives `str` pointing at the single byte `'0'`, so the octal branch is taken. It copies that first digit into `digs[0]`, increments `dno` to 1 and `i` to 1, and has now exhausted the only valid byte in the slice.

Root cause. The continuation test still probes `str[i]` for another octal digit but the helper has no remaining-size parameter and no `i < size` guard. After step 5, `i == 1` while only one byte was valid, so this condition asks for a second digit outside the slice. The patch changes this exact test to `i < size && octal_digit(str[i]) && dno < 3` and threads `size` into the helper.

Sink. Evaluating `str[1]` performs the actual out-of-bounds read. In the saved ASan run the helper was called on the final input byte, so `str[1]` is address `0x6020000000b5`, exactly 0 bytes to the right of the 5-byte testcase allocation `[0x6020000000b0, 0x6020000000b5)`.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the overread on the 5-byte heap buffer that libFuzzer allocates for this testcase before invoking the harness.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context is the libFuzzer testcase buffer, and the traced root cause explains why project code reads one byte past that external 5-byte region.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is source-grounded to this path: it adds a `size` parameter to `u8_read_escape_sequence()`, guards the octal/hex loops with `i < size`, and updates `flb_unescape_string_utf8()` to pass the remaining escape length before calling the helper. Stage 01 did not execute a fixed build for this sample, so `patch_resolves` remains false here.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42483517 run --version vulnerable --expect crash` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` with stack `u8_read_escape_sequence -> flb_unescape_string_utf8 -> logfmt_parser -> flb_parser_logfmt_do -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, matching OSS-Fuzz issue 42483517.

format.name: 5-byte logfmt fragment with unterminated quoted octal escape
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 5-byte blob stored in `poc` (SHA-256 `a8e9a4e3b07fd9f502e2768eda5a04779a20273cac60fd9d64427f4df7a17bb6`). Interpreted by the plain logfmt parser, it is one identifier byte `0xff`, followed by `=`, an opening quote, a backslash, and a single octal digit `0`, with no closing quote and no second escape digit. This makes `logfmt_parser()` materialize `key_len = 1`, `value = "\\0"`, `value_escape = FLB_TRUE`, and `value_len = 2`; `flb_unescape_string_utf8()` then forwards the one-byte suffix `'0'` into `u8_read_escape_sequence()`, which probes `str[1]` for another octal digit. Stage 01 only proves this exact blob and observed path; this contract does not generalize to nearby logfmt fragments, alternate leading identifier bytes, or other truncated escape forms.
